_comment: Cases that are NOT defects. Every probe listed here must answer 0 (clean) or
3 (could not measure) — never 1. An exit of 1 is a claim that a real reader
hit a real problem, and on these inputs that claim is false.
This is probe PRECISION, and until 2026-09-19 nothing measured it. The weekly
falsifiability job proves a probe CAN fail (MUTATE); the daily job proves it
passes on a healthy production. Neither catches the failure that actually
happened: verify-dead-click-target reported the survey consent gate as a dead
control because its button is deliberately disabled until both consent boxes
are ticked. Correct behaviour, reproduced convincingly, and D1 is in
AUTO_PR_CRITERIA — so it would have opened a draft pull request arguing
against correct behaviour on every run. It was caught by hand, which does not
scale and is the whole reason a human is still in this loop.
Add a case here whenever a probe is found reporting something that is not a
defect. That turns a one-off catch into a permanent guard.

cases.why: A tap on a paragraph is not a defect — the scanner prompt's HARD RULE says so and the probe is supposed to agree. 807 of 827 sessions with a dead_click are exactly this.

The consent gate's 'I agree' is disabled until both boxes are ticked. That is correct, and the button now says why via aria-describedby. A blocked control that explains itself is not a dead end. THIS IS THE CASE THAT WAS WRONG.
A live, reachable control on the survey intro.
A selector that matches nothing must be INCONCLUSIVE, never a reproduction.
Finishing the survey and pressing back shows the 'already finished' screen. Fixed 2026-09-17 and must stay fixed.
A valid report must never offer 'Take the survey' as the only way forward.

A reader whose only dead taps were on prose. On 2026-09-24 the replay pressed whatever covered their taps, followed an unlock control out to Stripe, and called Stripe's loading screen a stranded overlay: the pipeline's first reproduction PR (#282), posted under this reader. It must stay clean.
